donald-trump.title: Donald Trump
donald-trump.body:
Donald Trump is the President of the United States whose second-term agenda dominates the July 28, 2026 Badlands Brief across election administration, artificial intelligence policy, relations with [[israel|Israel]] and [[turkey|Turkey]], and the campaign against Mexican drug cartels.[{n}]

## Election administration order

A federal appeals court blocked key portions of Trump's executive order on election administration in 23 Democrat-led states, ruling the administration cannot enforce several provisions while litigation continues.[{n}] The order sought to impose new federal election requirements including proof-of-citizenship measures and restrictions affecting [[mail-in-voting|mail voting]], directing the [[department-of-homeland-security|Department of Homeland Security]] to compile lists of confirmed citizens eligible to vote, the [[united-states-postal-service|US Postal Service]] to set new standards for mail-in ballots, and the [[department-of-justice|Justice Department]] to prioritize investigations of state and local election officials issuing federal ballots to ineligible people.[{n}] The decision preserved Judge [[indira-talwani|Talwani]]'s injunction for the plaintiff states and set up a likely [[supreme-court-of-the-united-states|Supreme Court]] showdown over the scope of presidential authority in regulating federal elections.[{n}] Badlands commentary held that the dispute is about presidential authorities, that such battles have largely been going Trump's way, and that this one should as well — asking who is constitutionally authorized to exercise the Postal Service's decision rights if neither the states nor the President may.[{n}]

## Artificial intelligence

[[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] argued that Trump is "very clearly pinning a good degree of his futurism goals" on the perpetuation and acceleration of AI, a fact he said much of the [[truth-community|Truth Community]] misses amid anxiety about the industry's leading personalities.[{n}] Trump's Commerce Secretary [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]] reportedly said the administration aims to "protect open source AI," and former AI and Crypto Czar [[david-sacks|David Sacks]] argued that [[openai|OpenAI]] and [[anthropic|Anthropic]] seek regulation to stave off competitors.[{n}] Burning Bright further argued that [[china|China]]'s timed releases of open-weight models grant Trump the narrative shielding required to resist the regulation push, closing with the remark that it is a "good thing Trump and [[xi-jinping|Xi]] are Sovereign Bros."[{n}]

## Israel and Turkey

Trump praised Turkey as a "tremendous ally" while publicly criticizing Israeli military operations during a meeting with [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]], underscoring visible policy differences even as the US-Israel alliance remained intact.[{n}] [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] read this as a repeat of a September 2025 pattern in which Trump invited [[recep-tayyip-erdogan|Recep Tayyip Erdogan]] to the White House the day before Netanyahu addressed the UN General Assembly, and argued that Trump's plan is not kinetic war against Israel but the destruction of Israel's public reputation "by feeding into its greatest indulgences and allowing it the space to show the world what it truly is."[{n}]

## Cartels and Mexico

Media coverage increasingly portrayed the administration's intensified campaign against Mexican drug cartels — expanded intelligence operations, increased surveillance, and the designation of several cartels as foreign terrorist organizations — as laying groundwork for possible US military action inside [[mexico|Mexico]].[{n}] The administration maintained its focus is dismantling transnational criminal organizations responsible for fentanyl trafficking, human smuggling and violence, emphasizing cooperation with Mexico while declining to rule out further measures against cartel leadership.[{n}] GhostofBasedPatrickHenry noted the administration had indicted ten Mexican government officials over alleged [[sinaloa-cartel|Sinaloa cartel]] ties amid growing tension with Mexican President [[claudia-sheinbaum|Claudia Sheinbaum]], whom Trump accused of being a cartel puppet.[{n}]

supreme-court-of-the-united-states.title: Supreme Court of the United States
supreme-court-of-the-united-states.body:
The Supreme Court of the United States is the nation's highest court and the expected final arbiter of the 2026 litigation over President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s executive order on election administration.[{n}]

## Trump election order

After a federal appeals court blocked key portions of the order in 23 Democrat-led states, reporting described the decision as setting up a likely Supreme Court showdown over the scope of presidential authority in regulating federal elections and the balance of power between the federal government and the states.[{n}] Badlands commentary observed that the Court would be deciding "dangerously close to the midterms" — exactly the drama expected from what the Brief calls fake election narratives — and noted that history suggests the justices decline to make changes so close to an election, while allowing that "they've surprised us before."[{n}] The underlying question posed was constitutional: if the states lack authority over the [[united-states-postal-service|US Postal Service]] and the President does too, who is authorized to exercise its decision rights.[{n}]

mail-in-voting.title: Mail-In Voting
mail-in-voting.body:
Mail-in voting is the practice of casting ballots by post rather than in person, a persistent focus of election-integrity disputes in American politics and the core subject of the 2026 litigation over President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s executive order on election administration.[{n}]

## 2026 executive order litigation

Trump's order sought to impose new federal election requirements, including proof-of-citizenship measures and restrictions affecting mail voting.[{n}] Among its provisions, it instructed the [[united-states-postal-service|US Postal Service]] to establish new standards for mail-in ballots, directed the [[department-of-homeland-security|Department of Homeland Security]] to compile lists of confirmed US citizens eligible to vote and provide them to states, and directed the [[department-of-justice|Justice Department]] to prioritize investigations into state and local election officials who issue federal ballots to people deemed ineligible.[{n}] A federal appeals court blocked key portions of the order in 23 Democrat-led states in July 2026, keeping Judge [[indira-talwani|Talwani]]'s injunction intact pending litigation and setting up a probable [[supreme-court-of-the-united-states|Supreme Court]] fight whose resolution could land close to the midterm elections.[{n}]
